descriptions.text: The pool balance can be manipulated due to pair addresses not _isExcluded addresses. Vulnerable code snippet: https://bscscan.com/address/0x0025b42bfc22cbba6c02d23d4ec2abfcf6e014d4#code#L523 https://bscscan.com/address/0x0025b42bfc22cbba6c02d23d4ec2abfcf6e014d4#code#L646 The attacker flash loaned some $WBNB, bought some Sheep tokens, and burned the tokens in the attack contract by repeatedly calling the burn function. This results in a decrease in _tTotal and a larger return value for _getrate, which led to a gradual decrease in the pool balance. The remaining tokens were then swapped for a large amount of WBNB at a high price. Attack tx: https://bscscan.com/tx/0x61293c6dd5211a98f1a26c9f6821146e12fb5e20c850ad3ed2528195c8d4c98e Analysis: https://twitter.com/BlockSecTeam/status/1623999717482045440 https://twitter.com/BlockSecTeam/status/1624077078852210691

On February 10, 2023, the Sheep reflective BEP-20 token on BNB Chain was exploited via a liquidity pool accounting flaw, resulting in a reported loss of around $3,000. The root cause was the improper handling of tax redistribution which led to a mismatch between the pool's actual token balance and its recorded reserve, allowing attackers to withdraw the surplus using the skim function. The Sheep token's reflective tax mechanism caused an increase in the LP pair's token balance without updating its internal reserve.
